notes:
Round 3 of the post-acceptance BIO-OPS-002 remediation, following Kemi's own architecture ruling (relayed by god) rather than another independent narrowing guess on my part - this round was explicitly mechanical, not a design decision for me to make.

SY-OPS002-05: no code change required. Kemi ruled this a narrow, disclosed residual under ADR-0003 Decision 7, landing an ADR addendum in parallel (Zainab confirming) rather than asking for a code fix. Left as-is; my own DemoSessionContextAuditEndpoints.cs header already discloses the relevant limitation (previous_* fields are self-reported, not independently re-verified) and nothing in this round changes that disclosure's substance.

SY-OPS002-06 (High): Kemi's ruling required deleting the bespoke DemoSessionContextAuditEvent/IDemoSessionContextAuditSink/InMemoryDemoSessionContextAuditSink types built in rounds 1-2 (which had followed every other feature-project's own established per-feature audit-type convention) and reusing the SHARED Biolog.Api.Audit.AuditEvent/IAuditSink/InMemoryAuditSink/AuditActor/AuditTarget directly instead, since this event carries no classified value and needs no projection/redaction machinery a bespoke type would have genuinely required elsewhere.

Implemented exactly as specified: deleted all three bespoke files. Extended the shared AuditEvent (api/Biolog.Api/Audit/AuditEvent.cs) with an optional Device field (always null here) and an allowlisted Detail dict (IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>, defaulting to empty) - both backward compatible, confirmed by the full zero-regression test run that every existing caller (DeviceService, DeviceCertificationService) is unaffected. previous_tenant_id/previous_role_id/previous_actor_id/new_role_id now live in Detail - the same 'internal technical metadata' convention PhotoQualityAuditEventBuilder/PhotoAuditEventBuilder already use on their OWN bespoke event types (read both files directly before implementing, not assumed), applied to the shared type for the first time. new_tenant_id stays the event's own required TenantId since it genuinely is this event's tenant, not merely incidental detail. Classification is a literal 'internal' (not a computed rank) since every Detail field here is uniformly internal-only metadata - no field needs a higher rank the way a classified-value feature's own builder would compute. CorrelationId now validated against the canonical evt_ shape via Biolog.Api.Identifiers.CanonicalId.IsWellFormed (already used by DeviceService/DeviceCertificationService for the identical purpose, read directly before reusing) - an arbitrary caller-supplied X-Correlation-Id is discarded and a fresh evt_ minted instead of passed through, never trusted as-is.

DI registration caught a real, documented landmine before it could become a NEW finding: DeviceCertificationModule.cs's own header already discloses that a second AddSingleton<IAuditSink, ...>() anywhere would silently shadow DeviceRegistryModule's own registration (ASP.NET Core resolves one interface slot to whichever module registered it LAST, not a second independent one). Read that header directly before registering anything, and registered InMemoryAuditSink by its CONCRETE type (services.AddSingleton<InMemoryAuditSink>()) in TenantModule instead of through the shared IAuditSink interface slot - reuses the real shared type exactly as Kemi specified, without colliding with DeviceRegistry's own registration. Added a matching try/catch for AuditUnavailableException in the endpoint handler, mirroring DeviceRegistryModule's own identical catch (503 audit_unavailable) rather than leaving it to surface as an unhandled 500 - caught by re-reading that module's own endpoint code before considering the ADR-0003 Decision 7 AuditAsync port complete.

Verification: dotnet build clean (0 warnings/errors) - confirmed by rebuilding the EXACT committed tree after an amend (see process note below), not just the working tree before committing. All 9 of rounds 1-2's own DemoSessionContextAuditEndpointsTests passed UNMODIFIED against the rewritten implementation - the HTTP response shape (event_id/new_tenant_id/new_role_id/new_actor_id) is unchanged, so no test edits were needed, a good sign the externally-visible contract genuinely didn't change even though the internal audit plumbing did. Full Biolog.IntegrationTests 288/288 (unchanged), Biolog.UnitTests 211/211 (unchanged), module-reference/contract-freeze/secret-scan all PASS.

Process note: the first attempt to commit this round's changes used a single `git add` call that also named a non-existent directory pathspec, which failed the ENTIRE add silently for every other path in that call - the resulting commit captured only the three file deletions (git rm'd separately beforehand) and not the actual replacement code, leaving that one commit's own tree in a non-building state. Caught immediately via `git status`/`git show --stat` before this commit was ever reported anywhere or reviewed by anyone; amended in place (not a second corrective commit) since nothing had seen or built against the broken intermediate state yet, then rebuilt the amended tree from a clean `dotnet build` to confirm the fix actually landed, rather than trusting the second `git add` succeeded just because the command returned.

Orchestration: still DONE status, late-commit/builder-complete both refuse as in rounds 1-2 - committed directly on feature/BIO-TEN-002, tracked via this third per-round evidence file. Routed per god's relay: Zainab reviews given this round's audit-shape, then back to Seyi for AC04.
